title: The cut and the macOS stage call devbin's own built-ins through the project's launcher, so a project command at one of those names stands in for the core's verb (0335's shadow class beyond cache)
body:
Filed for devbin 0.1.27's batch (vc's decision 205, which carries vc's todo 214), from vc's archived todo 206: devbin-cc's reading of 2026-11-12, beside 0335.

## What happens

Issue 0335 found that the core reached its own `cache` verb through the project's launcher, so a project command named cache stood in for it, and fixed that verb: `core_verb` runs a verb of CORE_VERBS by its own path (lib/helpers:3743-3773), doctor fails a project command at such a name (lib/cmd/doctor:689-704), and config validation refuses a handler or run for one (lib/config:2001). CORE_VERBS holds cache alone (lib/helpers:3752).

The cut and the macOS stage still call other built-ins through `bin/devbin`, where a project handler of the same name shadows the built-in totally (lib/resolve:1039, AC-04.4):

- lib/cmd/release:3269, the stamp step: `gate_exec "$launcher" version set "$v"`.
- lib/cmd/release:3793, the formula step: `"$PROJECT_ROOT/bin/devbin" formula publish --pull`.
- lib/cmd/release:3960 and :3993, the macOS stage's publish: `macos bin-publish` and `macos publish`.
- lib/cmd/release:1377 and :2358: `ci-state --runs` and `ci-state --fires`.
- lib/cmd/macos:1549 and :1796: `release attach`, from publish and bin-publish.
- lib/cmd/macos:1820-1828, the macOS leg: `macos app-sign`, `bin-sign`, `app-notarize` and `bin-notarize`.

doctor's shadow check lists a project command at any of these names as a shadow, a note and not a failure (lib/cmd/doctor:719-730), since none is in CORE_VERBS.

## Not yet known

- Which of these a project is meant to override. Some may be meant as seams: a project with its own version scheme may own `version set`, and a project `cmd/release` shadows every release verb by design (0327's text). Others, such as `ci-state` and the macOS signing steps, read as the core's own.
- Whether any estate has a project command at one of these names today.

## Options, none chosen

- Sort each call site into the core's own, which joins CORE_VERBS, is called through core_verb and fails doctor when shadowed, or a declared seam, named in the docs as one so doctor's note is right.
- Leave the calls as they are, and say in the docs which built-ins a cut reaches through the launcher, so a project command at one of those names is a known override.

## Resolution

cc, 2026-11-17 16:52Z by date -u: fixed by unit 0365-1, landed at 77b6ec20 for 0.1.27, from 24b0fbab, stacked on 0364-1. The second option, docs only, on vc's word: no call changes. The core's rule is defaults with override, and the override is in use. A read-only fleet audit found six estates owning a macos command of their own, Intent's answering leg, publish and app-sign itself, the subverbs the cut's macOS stage and the built-in leg call through bin/devbin, and one estate owning release and formula; none owns version or ci-state. A call by path would put devbin's built-in where a live estate's own signer stands. The cut's calls go through no one helper, so the docs carry the list. configuration.md, after the cut's steps, names each built-in a cut reaches through bin/devbin with its step: version set (stamp); ci-state --runs and --fires (legs); macos leg, bin-publish and publish (the macOS stage and the release object) and, inside macos leg, app-sign, bin-sign, app-notarize and bin-notarize; release attach (from macos publish and bin-publish); formula publish --pull (formula step). A project command at one of those names replaces it in the cut too, as when a person runs it, and doctor names it as a shadow; cache alone is called by its own path (0335). The macOS page says a cut reaches macos through bin/devbin too, so a project's own macos or release replaces devbin's there as well. version set's override fails safe: the stamp step reads the stamp back with the core's reader and refuses one that did not take.

One arm in documentation.bats: configuration.md's paragraph names each of those verbs and that cache alone is called by its own path, and the macOS page says a project's own macos or release replaces devbin's. It was red at the base and green at the tip under BSD and GNU, documentation.bats whole 37 of 37, test scans 61 of 61 and check lint 0 breaches over 59 files (Desk slot 01M7N5T1FAGYCZATFWEZ3YPGPT). The first run (slot 01M7N31QPWEMRTKCXAY378ABHQ) failed two tree scans on the page's sentence, which cited an issue number; the unit was amended to drop it.
